question: The 2012 World Intellectual Property Organization Beijing Treaty1 grants performers in the audiovisual sector essential and long overdue protection and guarantees that European actors receive this protection when their work is used outside of the EU. The EU signed the treaty on 19 June 20132, but has still not ratified it. Ratification is necessary to protect European actors’ rights outside of the EU.

It offers an opportunity for the EU to remedy discriminations such as the shorter period of protection that actors enjoy (50 years) compared to musicians (70 years). On 11 May 2021, Commissioner Breton, in answer to Written Question E-000879/20213, informed Parliament that: ‘…the ratification will require the adoption of a Commission proposal by the Council with the consent of the European Parliament.
The Commission is committed to launching this process during the current mandate’. Three years later, the Commission is apparently yet to launch this process. 1.
Will the Commission honour its commitment and launch the process during the current mandate?
How does the Commission justify its part in making performers wait more than 10 years to receive this vital and totally deserved protection?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.6.2024) On 25 November 2020, the Commission indicated in its Action plan on intellectual property1, that ‘it will also work towards securing the EU's ratification of the World Intellectual Property Organisation Beijing Treaty (signed by the EU in 2013), which grants international protection to audio-visual performances’.

The Treaty aims at ensuring that audiovisual performers, who already enjoy a high level of protection in the EU, are adequately protected when audiovisual works containing their performance are exploited in third countries.

In line with the Commission’s reply to written question E-000879/2021, the Commission services have started discussing important aspects of the Beijing Treaty within the Copyright Council Working Party.

The discussion brought to the fore existing differences at national level regarding certain rights granted to audiovisual performers, in particular the right of communication to the public, as well as complex questions regarding the implications of a future conclusion.
The Commission remains committed to continue the process towards the conclusion of the Beijing Treaty in accordance with Article 218(6) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU2.
